description_full: The RMR Group Inc., through its subsidiary, The RMR Group LLC, provides real estate asset management services in the United States. The company offers management services to its four publicly traded real estate investment trusts, two real estate operating companies, and private capital vehicles. It also provides advisory services to publicly traded mortgage real estate investment trust. In addition, the company provides management services to a wide range of real estate assets and businesses that include healthcare facilities, senior living and other apartments, hotels, office buildings, industrial buildings, leased lands, net-lease service-focused retail, multifamily residential communities, and various specialized properties. The company was formerly known as REIT Management & Research Inc. and changed its name to The RMR Group Inc. in October 2015. The RMR Group Inc. was founded in 1986 and was incorporated on May 28th, 2015 in Maryland, USA and is headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts.

CEO compensation is 4× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (6/10).
financial_summary: The RMR Group Inc. is a micro-cap real estate business with a $266M market cap on $700M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -6% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -5.4pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 176% against a 9% cost of capital — a 167-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $72M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.30× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.1% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 9.7×.

Management returns a meaningful 11.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 4.7% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
